ranking.why: The patient fact of strong immunoreactivity for CD31, CD99, and Fli-1, and the reference material of Solitary Fibrous Tumor/Hemangiopericytoma having similar immunohistochemical staining patterns, supports this diagnosis.

The patient fact of left tentorial extra-axial enhancing mass and the reference material of Hemangiopericytoma being a slow-growing fibroblastic tumor with a large, solid, and highly vascularized mass, supports this diagnosis.

The patient fact of strong immunoreactivity for CD31, CD99, and Fli-1, and the reference material of Solitary Fibrous Tumor having similar immunohistochemical staining patterns, supports this diagnosis.
The patient fact of left occipital intracerebral hematoma and the reference material of Meningioma not typically presenting with hemorrhage, rules out this diagnosis.

The patient fact of no mention of immunosuppression or cutaneous lesions, and the reference material of Kaposi's Sarcoma typically occurring in patients with immunosuppression, rules out this diagnosis.
The patient fact of left tentorial extra-axial enhancing mass and the reference material of Hemangioma not typically presenting as an extra-axial mass, rules out this diagnosis.
The patient fact of left occipital intracerebral hematoma and the reference material of Cavernous Angioma not typically presenting with acute hemorrhage, rules out this diagnosis.
The patient fact of no mention of a primary tumor and the reference material of Metastasis not providing enough information to support or rule out this diagnosis.
The patient fact of no mention of lymphatic or renal involvement and the reference material of Lymphoma typically presenting with lymphatic and renal involvement, rules out this diagnosis.
